response: Yes, blood pressure can change in treated hypertensive patients depending on whether it is measured by a physician or a nurse. Studies have shown that systolic blood pressure measured by a nurse is significantly lower than the readings obtained by a physician, and are almost identical to ambulatory blood pressure monitoring. This suggests that blood pressure determination by a nurse is a reliable method, not only for diagnosis but also for evaluating the level of control of blood pressure during the follow-up of treated hypertensive patients.
